DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome

The TORCH screen confirms a Rubella IgM positive result in the newborn, which is a specific marker for acute infection acquired in utero. Despite the premature birth, the presence of maternal IgM indicates the fetus was infected, making Congenital Rubella Syndrome the primary diagnosis over cellulitis. I will now request a complete ophthalmologic exam and a fundoscopic exam to look for cataracts and retinopathy, which are common sequelae of this condition.
